A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EAGER research, with matching authors, algorithms and core experiments. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original decoding experiments across four models and five benchmarks, entropy–accuracy correlations, and budget and temperature analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds threshold-selection robustness experiments and comparisons against ESC and DeepConf.

M1.justification: Entropy-triggered branching, prefix reuse, the sequence cap, and both label-free and label-aware budget reallocation remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 are reformatted, and total versus per-prompt budget notation is clarified. Revised threshold selection changes the experimental protocol rather than the decoding algorithm.

E1.justification: The five main evaluation benchmarks remain. v2 adds MATH-500 for calibration and uses MATH-500, GSM8K and ZebraLogic in the calibration-robustness study, extending auxiliary coverage to easier mathematics and logic puzzles without replacing the main benchmark suite.

E2.justification: v1 empirically compares EAGER variants primarily with FULL PARALLEL sampling. v2 Appendix C and Table 5 add evaluated ESC and DeepConf-online comparisons on AIME 2025 across all four models. DeepConf was discussed but not experimentally compared in v1.

E3.justification: v1 reports benchmark-specific thresholds and fixes the EAGER-adapt comparison threshold at 2.0. v2 instead specifies per-model thresholds selected on 10 MATH-500 examples and transferred unchanged across benchmarks. It also introduces validation-source testing and wall-clock evaluation, with explicit comparator budgets and warm-up accounting. This establishes a reported protocol revision, not that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix B tests whether threshold selection transfers across validation sources and sampled subsets, using Qwen3-4B and both initialization and full variants. This directly examines calibration portability beyond v1's threshold sweeps. Existing budget-scaling and temperature analyses are retained; the temperature appendix moves from B to D.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports five randomly sampled validation sets per source and variant, totaling 30 selection runs, with threshold-selection frequencies in Table 4. This adds repeated-sampling information for calibration, but does not introduce repeated-run uncertainty estimates for the main performance results. Figure 2's correlation significance reporting is retained.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figure 3 report substantially revised performance and token counts. For example, SmolLM EAGER-init AIME 2025 Pass@k changes from 0.53 to 0.43 alongside a threshold change from 2.4 to 2.5, so this is not a same-setting deterioration. New Tables 4–5 add selection frequencies, comparator scores and runtimes. The complete threshold-sweep Table 3 and temperature results in v1 Table 4/v2 Table 6 are numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The entropy and peak-entropy definitions and budget-cap mathematics remain equivalent. Distinguishing total budget from its uniformly distributed per-prompt share clarifies an existing allocation description. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The training-free entropy-guided generation and adaptive-compute contributions remain. The abstract re-scopes quantitative gains to AIME 2025, reporting 59% rather than 65% fewer tokens with labels and explicitly stating label-free gains. The introduction's label-free performance-improvement claim changes from 13% to 12%; the main contribution is not redefined.

C2.justification: v2 interprets calibration stability as evidence that thresholds are primarily model-dependent, replacing v1's emphasis on task and model dependence. It adds substantive limitations concerning calibration cost, larger models, agentic settings and non-verifiable generation. Appendix C also adds explanations of ESC's sequential runtime costs, DeepConf's redundant generations, and qualifications about system-dependent timing.

D1.justification: v2 documents the calibration source, sample size and per-model threshold values, plus ESC's eight-window setting and DeepConf-online's warm-up accounting. These extend reproducibility information for the revised evaluation. The code/data access information, 32k context limit, temperature 0.6 and top-p 0.95 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Li et al.'s ESC work and expands the comparison with already-cited DeepConf, emphasizing branching and reuse versus sequential stopping or truncation. The broader positioning relative to REBASE and sequence-level self-certainty remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and threshold discussion are revised, the latter moves into experimental settings, and Limitations, Impact Statement and two appendix sections are added. Algorithms receive more compact wording. Most existing introduction, method and results prose, and the main section sequence, remain intact.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column proceedings layout. Figure 1 is redrawn with numbered stages and vertically arranged panels, algorithms are reformatted, and Figure 3's display changes. Two tables are added, the threshold table is restructured around models, and several appendix tables are relocated.

improvement.justification: Held-out calibration and its robustness study improve the justification for threshold portability compared with v1's benchmark-specific choices. Added competing methods, runtime measurements and explicit applicability limits also strengthen the paper. These gains are constrained by reporting inconsistencies: v2 gives GPT-oss full EAGER AIME Pass@k as 0.93 in Table 2 but 0.97 in Table 5 without explaining different settings, and Appendix B describes one GSM8K exception where Table 4 reports two. The evidence supports a positive but limited overall improvement.
